title.en: The packet that was not what it said

text.en: You buy a packet of biscuits that is half-empty or a bulb that does not light. What can a consumer do? The law gives rights and a way to complain.

Markets can cheat consumers through low weights, adulteration, false advertising and high prices. So rules and awareness are needed.
The Consumer Protection Act 1986, known as COPRA, set up consumer courts at the district, state and national levels for settling disputes.
A consumer can file a complaint at the District Forum for claims up to a limit, then the State Commission, and then the National Commission.
Consumer rights include the right to safety, to be informed, to choose, to be heard or represented, to seek redressal and to consumer education.
The Right to Information Act of 2005 lets citizens ask for information from government departments, and it helps people question delays.
Quality marks such as ISI, Agmark and Hallmark show standard goods. Consumers should check labels, dates and bills.
Consumer organisations and consumer forums help people by guiding and representing them in courts.
Be an aware consumer: ask for a cash memo, check the price and quality, and complain when needed.
